A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 27 complete pages including Appendices A–H. Full text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content, equations, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original RFM and neural-network experiments on modular arithmetic, including learning curves, feature correlations, and regularization comparisons in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experimental outcomes, including grokking curves, feature visualizations, and supplementary experiments in Appendix Figures 1–6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the AGOP updates, kernel choices, neural-network architecture, and circulant-feature procedures are identical in both versions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same modular addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division tasks, plus the simultaneous modular-polynomial tasks in Appendix E. Moduli and test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Figure 4's kernel comparisons, Figure 7's neural-network input comparisons, and Appendix Figure 5's no-regularization, weight-decay, and AGOP-regularization comparison.

E3.justification: Training fractions, input encoding, model sizes, optimizers, training budgets, and evaluation metrics match throughout Sections 3–4 and Appendix B. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Both retain identical analyses of feature reordering, enforced circulant structure, simultaneous-task grokking, regularization, and training-fraction sensitivity, including Appendix Figures 1–6.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported results and plotted curves match. For example, Figure 6 retains NFM–AGOP correlations of 0.955, 0.942, 0.924, and 0.929 for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 5.1, Appendix G's lemmas and proofs, and Appendix H's low-rank constructions are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about non-neural grokking, feature learning, block-circulant structure, and connections to the Fourier Multiplication Algorithm.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations and qualifications, including the a posteriori nature of progress measures, the distinction between the theorem's construction and RFM, and limitations concerning emergence with model size.

D1.justification: Appendix B's implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware details are unchanged. The code-access statement and repository-link destination also match; no reproducibility information is added.

R1.justification: The same 46 references and associated research-positioning passages appear in both PDFs, with no added citations or revised novelty claims.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v2 dated 18 Oct 2024 to v3 dated 9 Jul 2025 and becomes a hyperlink. Manuscript wording, headings, and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Appendix Figures 1–6, Algorithm 1, captions, and page layouts are identical. The margin-stamp text update does not alter the document layout.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, experimental evidence, theory, reproducibility details, and visual presentation are unchanged, including the appendices. Updating the arXiv stamp, hyperlink, and bibliographic metadata produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
